story.iWant: scrape ESPN for team form data as a backup source
story.soThat: I have redundancy if API-Football fails
story.tasks:
- Task 1: Set up ESPN scraper infrastructure (AC: #1, #10) - Create `/src/bet_bot/data/fetchers/espn_scraper.py` module - Initialize httpx.AsyncClient for scraper (reuse global client from api_football.py) - Implement rate limiter for ESPN scraper (1 request per 2s, 30 per minute max) - Create ESPN URL builder function for constructing team statistics URLs - Document ESPN URL patterns and CSS selector targets
- Task 2: Implement HTML parsing with BeautifulSoup4 (AC: #2, #3, #5) - Install beautifulsoup4 in requirements.txt (add if not present) - Create helper function to parse match results table from ESPN HTML - Extract last 5-10 match results (W/D/L) from results table - Extract goals for and goals against averages from team statistics - Extract win percentage for different time windows - Handle missing HTML elements gracefully (return partial data, not None) - Handle malformed HTML without crashing (catch BeautifulSoup parsing errors) - Add logging for parsing operations (success, missing elements, errors)
- Task 3: Implement fetch_team_form_espn() function (AC: #3, #8, #9) - Create async function: `fetch_team_form_espn(team_name: str, league: str) -> Optional[TeamForm]` - Query ESPN for team statistics page - Parse HTML response to extract form data - Construct TeamForm object with scraped values - Validate constructed TeamForm against Pydantic model - Return TeamForm object on success, None on failure - Include timestamp in logs for performance tracking
- Task 4: Implement retry logic with timeout (AC: #4) - Use tenacity retry decorator (max 2 attempts, NOT 5) - Configure exponential backoff (1s, 2s base for short timeouts) - Set HTTP request timeout to 10s total (ESPN can be slow) - Implement custom retry condition for specific errors only - Don't retry on 403/404 (ESPN explicitly blocks scrapers sometimes) - Log retry attempts with context
- Task 5: Implement error handling and logging (AC: #5, #6, #9) - Create custom exception: `ScraperError` (if not already in exceptions.py) - Catch httpx.TimeoutException, httpx.ConnectError, httpx.NetworkError - Catch BeautifulSoup parsing errors (TypeError, AttributeError on missing elements) - Catch Pydantic ValidationError when constructing TeamForm - Log all errors with context: URL attempted, error type, error message - Return None for all error cases (graceful degradation) - Never expose raw stack traces (log full error but return None to caller)
- Task 6: Implement backup-only activation (AC: #7) - Create function: `fetch_team_form_with_fallback(team_id, league_id) -> Optional[TeamForm]` - In `/src/bet_bot/data/fetchers/__init__.py`: Try API-Football first, then ESPN - Call ESPN scraper ONLY if API-Football returns None - Log which source was used (API-Football or ESPN) - Update export in `__init__.py` to expose fallback function - Document in code that this is backup-only
- Task 7: Write unit and integration tests (AC: #2, #5, #8, #9) - Create `/tests/unit/test_espn_scraper.py` with mocked HTML responses - Test HTML parsing with sample ESPN page HTML - Test extraction of match results (W/D/L patterns) - Test goal average calculations - Test handling of missing HTML elements (graceful degradation) - Test handling of malformed HTML - Test retry logic: verify 2 attempts max, exponential backoff - Test rate limiting: verify 1 request per 2s enforced - Test TeamForm model mapping: verify all required fields populated - Test error handling: verify None returned for various error types - Test fallback behavior: verify ESPN called only if API-Football fails - Target 85%+ code coverage (slightly lower than API-Football due to scraper fragility)

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. Create `/src/bet_bot/data/fetchers/espn_scraper.py` module 2. Implement web scraping using BeautifulSoup4 for HTML parsing 3. Extract team form data from ESPN URLs: last 5-10 results, goals for/against, win percentage 4. Add retry logic (2 attempts with exponential backoff and timeout) 5. Handle HTML parsing errors gracefully (missing elements, malformed HTML) 6. Log scraping status (success/failure) with URL and error context 7. Never call ESPN scraper unless API-Football fails (backup-only activation) 8. Map scraped data to `TeamForm` model with all required fields 9. Return TeamForm object with validated data or None on failure 10. Implement rate limiting to avoid scraper being blocked (max 1 request per 2 seconds)

doc.title: Technical Specification
doc.snippet: ESPN scraper integration overview: Purpose is backup form data, head-to-head history if API-Football fails. Scraping strategy targets ESPN soccer URLs, extract results table, CSS selectors for team stats. Fragility is medium (ESPN redesigns occasionally, requires maintenance). Fallback: If scrape fails, continue without ESPN data (graceful degradation). Activation: ONLY call if API-Football form is missing or stale.

doc.title: Data Dictionary
doc.snippet: Team form data required: last_5_results, last_10_results (array[W/D/L]), win_percentage_5, win_percentage_10 (0.0-1.0 range), goals_for_avg_5, goals_for_avg_10, goals_against_avg_5, goals_against_avg_10. Freshness requirement: < 24h old (OK for ESPN since it's backup). Source: API-Football + ESPN. TeamForm model fields: team_id, team_name, last_5_results, last_10_results, win_percentage_5, win_percentage_10, goals_avg_home, goals_avg_away, goals_against_avg_home, goals_against_avg_away.

doc.title: Project Development Standards
doc.section: HTTP Client Architecture & Web Scraping Patterns
doc.snippet: CRITICAL MANDATORY: Use httpx.AsyncClient singleton (NOT requests or aiohttp). Use tenacity for retry logic with exponential backoff. Implement custom exception hierarchy for error handling. Validate response with Pydantic models. Use async/await for all I/O. Implement client-side rate limiting using token bucket algorithm. For web scrapers: Use BeautifulSoup4 for HTML parsing. Handle missing HTML elements gracefully (return partial data). Graceful degradation pattern: return None on failure, never crash pipeline.

doc.title: Development Stories
doc.section: Story 2.3: Implement ESPN Form Data Scraper
doc.snippet: User story: Scrape ESPN for team form data as backup source for redundancy. Acceptance criteria: Scraper module, HTML parsing, retry logic (2 attempts max), TeamForm mapping, backup-only activation. Definition of Done: Scraper works without crashing, handles missing elements, logs clearly when failing. Rate limiting: 1 request per 2 seconds (30 per minute max) to avoid ESPN blocking.

artifact.reason: Target model for scraper output. TeamForm requires: team_id, team_name, last_5_results, last_10_results, win_percentage_5, win_percentage_10, goals_avg_home, goals_avg_away, goals_against_avg_home, goals_against_avg_away. All fields have Pydantic validators. Scraper must construct valid TeamForm instances with all required fields populated.

Custom exception hierarchy for error handling. ScraperError already defined and ready to use. Pattern: log errors with context (url, reason), return None to caller, never raise to caller for backup sources. Validates error handling pattern across project.

HTTP client singleton pattern and rate limiter implementation to reuse. ESPN scraper must: (1) import and reuse get_http_client() from api_football.py, (2) implement separate RateLimiter for ESPN (1 req/2s = 30/min), (3) follow retry pattern using tenacity with 2 attempts max (NOT 5), (4) use same error handling pattern (return None, log with context).

Module exports and fallback pattern. After Story 2.3, this file must be updated to export fetch_team_form_with_fallback() function that calls API-Football first, then ESPN as backup. Pattern: "Try API-Football first, ESPN only if primary returns None."

Structured logging setup. ESPN scraper must use project logger for all operations: success/failure messages, retry attempts, parsing errors, rate limit waits. Follows project pattern of logging with context (URLs, error details, timestamps).

Configuration management pattern. Project uses Config class from environment variables. Scraper doesn't need new API keys (ESPN doesn't require authentication), but follows pattern of accessing configuration via Config class.

python.usage: Async HTTP client for fetching ESPN pages. Reuse global singleton from api_football.py. Supports 10s timeout per request (ESPN slow). Handles TimeoutException, ConnectError, NetworkError.
HTML parsing library. Extract match results table, CSS selectors for team stats. Already in pyproject.toml dependencies. Handle missing elements gracefully (return [] or partial data, not crash).
Retry decorator with exponential backoff. Configure for 2 attempts max (NOT 5 like API-Football). Min/max backoff: 1s, 2s. Don't retry 403/404 (ESPN blocks). Already installed from Story 2.2.
Validate TeamForm model before returning. Catch ValidationError and return None gracefully. Already installed from Story 2.1.
Async/await patterns. Asyncio.Semaphore for rate limiting (implement token bucket). Asyncio.sleep for backoff delays.

story-context.constraints: - MANDATORY: Use httpx.AsyncClient singleton from api_football.py (ZERO tolerance for duplicate clients) - MANDATORY: Use tenacity @retry decorator for retry logic (NOT custom sleep/retry loops) - MANDATORY: Implement separate RateLimiter for ESPN (1 request per 2 seconds = 30/min max) - MANDATORY: Max 2 retry attempts for scraper (NOT 5 like API-Football) - MANDATORY: Don't retry 403/404 errors (ESPN blocks scrapers; retry only timeout/network errors) - MANDATORY: Return None on ANY failure (never raise exceptions to caller; graceful degradation) - MANDATORY: Validate all output with Pydantic TeamForm model before returning - MANDATORY: Use project logger for all operations (structured logging with context) - MANDATORY: BeautifulSoup4 must handle missing HTML elements gracefully (return partial data, not crash) - CODE STYLE: Type hints on all functions (async def fetch_team_form_espn(team_name: str, league: str) -> Optional[TeamForm]) - CODE STYLE: Docstrings on all public functions (explain ESPN-specific behavior: fragile, backup-only) - CODE STYLE: 10s HTTP timeout per request (ESPN is slower than API-Football) - TESTING: Minimum 85%+ code coverage (slightly lower than API-Football due to scraper fragility and HTML parsing complexity) - TESTING: Use mocked HTML responses in unit tests (don't hit ESPN during tests) - TESTING: Test graceful degradation: verify function returns None (not exception) for parsing failures

interface.signature: class RateLimiter: __init__(max_requests: int, time_window: int); async def acquire()

tests.standards: Framework: pytest with pytest-asyncio for async tests, pytest-cov for coverage. Target 85%+ code coverage (slightly lower than API-Football due to HTML parsing complexity and scraper fragility). Test structure: Unit tests in /tests/unit/test_espn_scraper.py with mocked HTML responses and network calls. Integration tests verify TeamForm model mapping. Mocking strategy: Mock httpx.AsyncClient.get() to return sample ESPN HTML responses, mock BeautifulSoup parsing. Error scenarios: Test all failure modes return None (not exception). Rate limiting: Use asyncio.sleep() mocks to verify timing. Logging verification: Capture logger output, verify messages include URLs and error context.
tests.locations: - /tests/unit/test_espn_scraper.py (primary unit tests with mocked responses) - /tests/integration/test_espn_integration.py (optional: integration with actual HTML samples) - Test fixtures: /tests/fixtures/espn_sample_html.html (sample ESPN team page)
